What Equation (7) says is that the derivative of the composite function ƒ(r(t)) is the “derivative” (gradient) of the outside function ƒ “times” (dot product) the derivative of the inside function r. This is analogous to the “Outside-Inside” Rule for derivatives of com- posite functions studied in Section 3.6. That is, the multivariable Chain Rule for paths has exactly the same form as the rule for single-variable differential calculus when appropriate interpretations are given to the meanings of the terms and operations involved.
